title: Step a first-order model
scope: Explicit Euler for a supplied toy model

items.prompt: A capacitor voltage y (V) decays as dy/dt = -k·y with k = 0.5 s⁻¹. Starting from y0 = 4 V, take ONE explicit Euler step of h = 0.2 s and return the next y. Do not use the exact exponential solution. Enter exact values as decimals or fractions such as 3/8; tolerance ±0.001.
items.solution: Slope f(4) = -0.5·4 = -2 V/s. y_next = 4 + 0.2·(-2) = 3.6 V. The exact solution 4·e^(-0.1) ≈ 3.619 V belongs to a different model; one Euler step is the requested numerical model.
hints: Explicit Euler uses only the slope at the current state: y_next = y0 + h·f(y0), where f(y) = -k·y.
Evaluate the slope f(y0) = -0.5·4 first (in V/s), then multiply it by h = 0.2 s and add the result to y0.
Slope f(4) = -0.5·4 = -2 V/s. y_next = 4 + 0.2·(-2) = 3.6 V. The exact solution 4·e^(-0.1) ≈ 3.619 V belongs to a different model; one Euler step is the requested numerical model.
items.remediation: If you got about 3.619 you used the exact exponential, not one Euler step. If you got 4.4 you dropped the minus sign in -k·y. Revisit /lessons/M07.

items.prompt: The state y (V) obeys dy/dt = -k·y + u with k = 2 s⁻¹ and a constant input u = 1 V/s. Starting from y0 = -3 V, take ONE explicit Euler step of h = 0.25 s and return the next y. Enter exact values as decimals or fractions such as 3/8; tolerance ±0.001.
hints: The state is negative, so -k·y is positive; the constant input u adds to the slope.
Evaluate the slope at y0 = -3 V as -2·(-3) + 1, watching the double negative, then advance by h = 0.25 s.
items.remediation: If you got -4.25 you used -k·y = -6 for y = -3 (a sign error with a negative state). If you got -1.5 you dropped the input u; -2.75 means you dropped the -k·y term. Revisit /lessons/M07.

items.prompt: A stiff decay dy/dt = -k·y has k = 4 s⁻¹ and y0 = 2 V. A coarse controller loop uses ONE explicit Euler step of h = 0.3 s. Return the next y exactly as explicit Euler computes it. Enter exact values as decimals or fractions such as 3/8; tolerance ±0.001.
items.solution: Slope = -4·2 = -8 V/s. y_next = 2 + 0.3·(-8) = -0.4 V. The sign flip is an artefact of the large step (h·k = 1.2 > 1); the exact solution 2·e^(-1.2) ≈ 0.602 V stays positive.
hints: Apply the same Euler formula even though h·k is greater than 1; the method itself decides the result.
Compute the slope -k·y0 at y0 = 2 V, multiply it by h = 0.3 s, and add it to y0 (equivalently y0·(1 - h·k) when u = 0).
Slope = -4·2 = -8 V/s. y_next = 2 + 0.3·(-8) = -0.4 V. The sign flip is an artefact of the large step (h·k = 1.2 > 1); the exact solution 2·e^(-1.2) ≈ 0.602 V stays positive.
items.remediation: If you reported about 0.602 V or clipped the result to 0 you replaced the Euler step with the exact behaviour. The question asks what explicit Euler returns, overshoot included. Revisit /lessons/M07.

items.prompt: A low-pass filter output y (V) obeys dy/dt = -y + 3 (k = 1 s⁻¹, input u = 3 V/s) with y0 = 1.5 V. Apply TWO explicit Euler steps of h = 0.05 s each and return y1 and y2. Enter exact values as decimals or fractions such as 3/8; tolerance ±0.001.
hints: Two Euler steps need two slope evaluations: one at y0 and a new one at y1.
Step 1: the slope at y0 is -1.5 + 3; multiply it by h = 0.05 and add it to y0 to get y1. Evaluate the slope again at y1 before taking step 2.
items.remediation: If y2 = 1.65 you reused the first slope, which is the same as one step of 2h = 0.1 s. Recompute the slope at y1. Revisit /lessons/M07.

items.prompt: A heater temperature offset y (K) obeys dy/dt = -k·y + u with k = 0.5 s⁻¹ and a constant cooling input u = -1 K/s, starting at y0 = 0.4 K. Apply TWO explicit Euler steps of h = 0.1 s and return y1 and y2. Enter exact values as decimals or fractions such as 3/8; tolerance ±0.001.
hints: Both terms of the slope are negative here, so y falls; recompute the slope after the first step.
Step 1: the slope at y0 is -0.5·0.4 + (-1). Take the step to get y1, then evaluate -0.5·y1 - 1 for step 2.
items.remediation: If y2 = 0.16 you reused the first slope -1.2 K/s. If y1 = 0.48 you added u = -1 with the wrong sign. Revisit /lessons/M07.

items.prompt: A motor speed y (rad/s) obeys dy/dt = -k·y + u with k = 3 s⁻¹ and u = 6 rad/s², starting from rest (y0 = 0). A coarse simulation applies TWO explicit Euler steps of h = 0.2 s. Return y1 and y2. Enter exact values as decimals or fractions such as 3/8; tolerance ±0.001.
items.solution: Slope at y0: -3·0 + 6 = 6 rad/s², so y1 = 0 + 0.2·6 = 1.2 rad/s. Slope at y1: -3·1.2 + 6 = 2.4 rad/s², so y2 = 1.2 + 0.2·2.4 = 1.68 rad/s. One step of 2h would give 2.4, and the exact solution 2·(1 - e^(-1.2)) ≈ 1.398 is a different model.
hints: The step is large (h·k = 0.6), so recomputing the slope at y1 changes y2 a lot.
Step 1 starts from rest, so the slope is just u. After finding y1, evaluate -3·y1 + 6 before step 2.

Slope at y0: -3·0 + 6 = 6 rad/s², so y1 = 0 + 0.2·6 = 1.2 rad/s. Slope at y1: -3·1.2 + 6 = 2.4 rad/s², so y2 = 1.2 + 0.2·2.4 = 1.68 rad/s. One step of 2h would give 2.4, and the exact solution 2·(1 - e^(-1.2)) ≈ 1.398 is a different model.
items.remediation: If y2 = 2.4 you reused the first slope (one step of 2h = 0.4 s). If y2 is about 1.398 you used the exact solution. Revisit /lessons/M07.

routeNotes.decay-state: Advance one explicit Euler step, including a negative state and a step that overshoots.
routeNotes.driven-response: Advance two driven-response steps, recomputing the slope after each step.
